lessons.title: Design an event contract

explanation.text: Product measurement is like a car dashboard: a few reliable indicators help you drive, while recording every movement distracts and increases risk. Here the part you will actually inspect is a typed view_product/add_to_cart event with a timestamp and no personal information; stop using the analogy if it obscures the technical boundary shown by the code.

explanation.title: Understand it deeply
explanation.text: Start by bounding this lesson’s case: a stable add_to_cart event containing useful product identifier and value without email, phone, or free text. Name events after user intent, define a small set of stable properties, and exclude identity, free text, and secrets from analytics payloads. The term event taxonomy is not a decorative label: A shared convention for names, properties, and meanings of measured events. It determines what enters, which authority may act, and which observation counts as evidence rather than an impression.

explanation.title: Understand it deeply

It shows why the professional correction is to centralize a typed, versioned contract, minimize properties, and test payloads before changing dashboards, not to conceal the error.

explanation.title: Understand it deeply
